highlights:
shows the winning party in each electorate in the current parliament at every federal election since 1984. In 1984, the House of Representatives was increased in size from 127 to 148. It is now 151. There have been fourteen federal elections since 1984 and the table is designed to give a pictorial overview of the results. Whilst there have ... The table demonstrates the stability inherent in the electoral system. Prior to the 2022 election, the table showed that 71 seats, representing 47.3% of the total, had been held by either the ALP or one of the coalition parties at ... Following the 2022 election, at which 18 seats changed hands, increased volatility and fragmentation of the vote is evident, as just 53 of the current seats have been held by the same party since 1984, or from the seat’s creation. The election delivered a majority Labor government with 77 seats, whilst the Liberal Party lost 18 seats – 10 to the ALP, 6 to independents and 2 to the Greens. The ALP had a net gain of eight, losing one to the Greens and one to an ... vote that began with the loss of Warringah in 2019. In addition, Higgins and Tangney were won by the ALP. Overall, however, just 12.58% of the 151 seats changed hands. In interpreting the table, it is important to bear in mind that some seats have undergone significant boundary changes as a result of redistributions every seven years.
